_comment: Authored analysis: ownership, lifecycle, refcount and locking judgements that no composer can derive, keyed to the C entities they describe. The structural half of each record (field layout, signatures, footprints, casts) is composed from the CodeQL tables on demand and merged in at read time, so a re-extract rewrites nothing here. Written only by `crustify-oracle <target> query {types,symbols} --update`; read through crustify.manifests. Hand-edit at your own risk: `--update` validates a submission against the composed skeleton (unknown field, wrong kind, ptr-invariant violation) and this file does not.

types.name: ACCESS_DESCRIPTION_st
types._comment_agent: ACCESS_DESCRIPTION is an ASN.1 SEQUENCE. Its generated destructor recursively releases both child pointers; public construction paths replace method and mutate location, and the published layout permits either slot to be cleared.

ptr.note: ACCESS_DESCRIPTION_new allocates the GENERAL_NAME child; construction code mutates it in place, and ACCESS_DESCRIPTION_free recursively releases any non-null installed child.
The sequence owns one ASN1_OBJECT_free obligation. The slot can contain a dynamic object or a static OBJ_nid2obj result (whose free is a no-op), and public field access can clear it.

types.name: ASN1_ITEM_st
types._comment_agent: ASN1_ITEM instances and every pointer they publish are immutable function-local static descriptors generated by asn1t.h macros; no lifecycle routine owns or releases the descriptor storage.

ptr.note: Optional process-lifetime descriptor selected by itype; it aliases a static ASN1_PRIMITIVE_FUNCS, ASN1_EXTERN_FUNCS, or ASN1_AUX value and is never freed through ASN1_ITEM.
All public ASN1_ITEM definition macros store a process-lifetime string literal; consumers use it directly as a non-null C string.
Process-lifetime static const template storage: null for types without templates, a singleton for ASN1_ITEM_TEMPLATE, or an array of tcount elements for SEQUENCE/CHOICE.

types.name: ASN1_TEMPLATE_st
types._comment_agent: ASN1_TEMPLATE values are generated as static const descriptors by the public asn1t.h macros. They own neither their item callback nor their field-name string. The item slot is a two-way discriminated union resolved through one function-pointer type: flags & ASN1_TFLG_ADB_MASK selects the ASN1_ADB reading, and is zero for an ordinary ASN1_ITEM.

ptr.note: ASN1_EX_TYPE and ASN1_EX_TEMPLATE_TYPE initialize this const char pointer with a stringized identifier, yielding a non-null immutable static NUL-terminated string.

ASN1_EX_TYPE and ASN1_EX_TEMPLATE_TYPE initialize this slot with ASN1_ITEM_ref(type) = type##_it; ASN1_ADB_OBJECT and ASN1_ADB_INTEGER initialize it with tblname##_adb. Both expand to a nullary function returning the address of static const storage, so the callable is non-null, immutable and process-lifetime borrowed. Its RESULT is discriminated, not the slot: flags & ASN1_TFLG_ADB_MASK nonzero means the returned pointer is an ASN1_ADB table rather than an ASN1_ITEM, which is exactly the test ossl_asn1_do_adb (crypto/asn1/tasn_utl.c:236), asn1_template_new (crypto/asn1/tasn_new.c:222) and asn1_item_embed_d2i (crypto/asn1/tasn_dec.c:402) apply before reading it.

types.name: ASN1_VALUE_st
types._comment_agent: Reviewed. OpenSSL deliberately never defines ASN1_VALUE_st; include/openssl/asn1.h only typedefs the tag, and the templates use its pointers as type-erased handles, so the type has no layout. Correcting the earlier claim that it also has no lifecycle: it has one, it is simply not recoverable from the pointer. ASN1_item_new / ASN1_item_new_ex construct a value and ASN1_item_free(val, it) releases it, both parameterized by the const ASN1_ITEM * template; crypto/asn1/tasn_fre.c forwards to ossl_asn1_item_embed_free(&val, it, 0), which walks `it` to reach every field, so the template is part of the destructor rather than a hint. The Rust owner is therefore a CBoxWith over a CDropper carrying that template, never a plain CBox with a CDropped impl; the wrap wave emits only the borrowed handles, because every ASN1_VALUE * this crate produces is reached through one of the concrete generated types the templates cast to and from, each already carrying its own wrapper and *_free. ASN1_item_dup is the matching deep copy but takes and returns void *, so it belongs to the void lifetime tier, not to this tag.

types.name: X509_algor_st
types._comment_agent: X509_ALGOR owns both pointer fields through its ASN.1 SEQUENCE template. X509_ALGOR_set0 transfers the algorithm object and parameter payload on success; sequence teardown releases algorithm with ASN1_OBJECT_free and the optional parameter with ASN1_TYPE_free. Direct code writes through parameter, while algorithm objects are treated as immutable after installation. Both slots can be null, but X509_ALGOR_new does not start null: the template installs the built-in OBJ_nid2obj(NID_undef) object. The record is also embedded by value (public NETSCAPE_SPKI.sig_algor; internal x509_st, x509_cinf_st, X509_req_st, X509_crl_st, X509_crl_info_st, X509_ACERT bodies) and built on the stack in crypto/evp/evp_lib.c; that embedded teardown runs inside the parent's ASN1_EMBED template and has no standalone C disposer.

ptr.note: Owned AlgorithmIdentifier OID slot. X509_ALGOR_set0 frees the old object and transfers aobj on success; ASN.1 sequence teardown calls ASN1_OBJECT_free. Built-in objects are accepted because that destructor is intentionally a no-op for non-dynamic objects, and X509_ALGOR_new installs one of them (OBJ_nid2obj(NID_undef)) rather than leaving the slot null; the stack instances in crypto/evp/evp_lib.c and the error path of ossl_X509_ALGOR_from_nid do leave it null. The template marks the field mandatory, so a null slot or a content-free OID makes asn1_ex_i2c return -1: i2d_X509_ALGOR and hence the encode/decode X509_ALGOR_dup both fail in that state, and OBJ_cmp inside X509_ALGOR_cmp would dereference the null. Callers read but do not mutate the installed ASN1_OBJECT pointee.

Optional owned ASN1_TYPE. X509_ALGOR_set0 allocates, replaces, or frees it according to ptype, and sequence teardown releases it; multiple users update its discriminator and active payload in place. The ASN1_OPT template omits a null slot from the encoding, so unlike algorithm a null parameter keeps the identifier encodable. The one exception to the owning contract is the hand-built stack X509_ALGOR in crypto/evp/evp_lib.c, which points parameter at a caller-owned ASN1_TYPE and is abandoned without teardown.

ptr.note: Mandatory ASN1_SIMPLE child owned by the extension; full destruction releases its free obligation and set_object replaces the slot with an OBJ_dup result. The pointee remains shared because built-in objects may be static.

Mandatory ASN1_SIMPLE field initialized by X509_NAME_ENTRY_new; the entry owns and mutates the ASN1_STRING and X509_NAME_ENTRY_free releases it.

Optional non-owning library context retained by new_ex/set0_libctx and passed into later decoder construction; no up-ref or free is performed, so the external context must remain live while the pubkey may use it.

Optional cached EVP_PKEY. The pubkey owns one reference: decode creates it and X509_PUBKEY_set takes an up-ref before storing it; x509_pubkey_ex_free pays that debt with EVP_PKEY_free. X509_PUBKEY_get0 exposes a mutable borrowed handle.
Optional NUL-terminated property query deep-copied with OPENSSL_strdup and released with OPENSSL_free; consumers only read it as a string.

Unique ASN1_BIT_STRING child allocated/populated during construction, mutated by public-key setters and decoding, duplicated deeply, and released by ASN1_BIT_STRING_free. It is transiently null only in partial construction.

types.name: _IO_FILE
types._comment_agent: Reviewed as an imported, permanently C-owned type. Its footprint is opaque everywhere: opaque_in is complete for the tree, and the only field touchers are glibc's own inline helpers in bits/stdio.h (getc_unlocked, putc_unlocked, feof_unlocked, ferror_unlocked), none of which this codebase calls. No OpenSSL, apps, ssl or test code reads or writes a single member, so the wrapper keeps the layout opaque and exposes no field accessors; the field judgements below record glibc's documented internal contract so that a later wave cannot mistake an interior pointer for owned storage. Stream lifecycle stays in libc: fopen/fdopen allocate and fclose releases. libcrypto never frees a stream it did not open (BIO_new_file opens and closes its own; BIO_new_fp and BIO_set_fp free the caller's stream only when the caller passes BIO_CLOSE), so the type has borrowed handles and no owning pointer form until an fclose-backed release strategy is scheduled.

ptr.note: First valid character of the backup area; an interior pointer into the _IO_save_base allocation, null when no backup area exists.

Start of the reserve area, with runtime-conditional ownership: normally a glibc-allocated buffer released when the stream is closed or re-buffered, but setvbuf can install caller storage and an unbuffered stream points at the inline _shortbuf member instead. The flag deciding which case applies is glibc-internal, so no wrapper may free this slot; null until the stream is buffered.
End of the reserve area started by _IO_buf_base; a bound rather than storage of its own, null while the stream has no buffer.
Start of the putback+get area inside the reserve area; interior pointer, null before a buffer exists, never released on its own.
End of the get area inside the reserve area; interior pointer maintained by glibc on every refill, null before a buffer exists, and never released on its own.

Current read position inside the reserve area delimited by _IO_buf_base/_IO_buf_end; glibc advances it and refills through it, and it is null while the stream has no buffer. It is an interior pointer, never separately allocated or released.

Start of the saved (non-current) get area allocated by glibc when the stream switches to its backup area; released by glibc when the backup area is discarded or the stream is closed. Null whenever no backup area exists, which is the state for every stream this tree opens.
End of the saved get area; a bound on the _IO_save_base allocation, null when no backup area exists.
Start of the put area inside the reserve area; glibc writes bytes through it when flushing, and it is null before a buffer exists.
End of the put area inside the reserve area; compared against _IO_write_ptr to decide when to overflow. Interior pointer, null before a buffer exists.
Current put position inside the reserve area; the __putc_unlocked_body macro stores through it and advances it. Interior pointer, null before a buffer exists.
Link into glibc's global list of open streams. Each linked stream is owned by whoever opened it, so following the chain must never transfer ownership; null at the end of the list.

Conversion state used once a stream acquires wide orientation; glibc attaches storage that lives with the stream's own allocation and mutates it while converting. Not separately released, and null for byte-oriented streams, which is every stream this tree opens.

Type-erased buffer the stream registers for release during glibc's process-teardown pass rather than at fclose. Ownership sits with the stream implementation; no code in this tree reads, writes or frees it, and it is null for ordinary streams.
Link into glibc's process-teardown (__libc_freeres) chain of streams. The linked stream belongs to whoever opened it, so this is a borrow; null outside that teardown bookkeeping.

Opaque _IO_lock_t (a void typedef outside libc) guarding the stream. glibc allocates it together with the stream, or points at static storage for the standard streams, and releases it with the stream; it is written by every locked stdio operation and is never freed through this field. The header's flag documentation (_IO_USER_LOCK) shows the slot is implementation-managed, and it can be null for a stream glibc has not finished initializing.

Head of the intrusive list of stream markers. A marker is created and destroyed by the code that registers it (the C++ streambuf protocol this layout preserves); closing the stream detaches the list without freeing its nodes, so the field borrows rather than owns. Null for every stream this tree opens.

Wide-character buffer state that glibc allocates together with the stream and tears down with it, so the slot must not be released on its own. Written throughout wide-oriented I/O; null when a stream carries no wide state.

types.name: addrinfo
types._comment_agent: Reviewed 2026-08-23 against /usr/include/netdb.h and crypto/bio/bio_addr.c. The releaser is selected by the PRODUCER, not by the node: a chain from getaddrinfo must be released with freeaddrinfo, and every chain returned by BIO_lookup/BIO_lookup_ex must be released with BIO_ADDRINFO_free. BIO_ADDRINFO_free itself dispatches on bai_family - it forwards resolver chains to freeaddrinfo and walks the AF_UNIX nodes it allocated itself - so one owner strategy covers both kinds of OpenSSL list, and the layout still binds no unconditional CDropped because nothing in a node identifies its producer. addrinfo_wrap leaves ai_addrlen and ai_canonname zero, so BIO_ADDRINFO_sockaddr_size reports 0 for those nodes.

ptr.note: Optional socket address of ai_addrlen bytes owned by the node. freeaddrinfo releases it with a resolver chain; a node built by addrinfo_wrap instead holds a BIO_ADDR from BIO_ADDR_new that BIO_ADDRINFO_free releases with OPENSSL_free, which is why the two origins cannot share one releaser. Consumers only read it: BIO_ADDRINFO_address and BIO_ADDRINFO_sockaddr both return it as const.

Optional NUL-terminated canonical name owned by a resolver-produced node and released by freeaddrinfo together with its chain. OpenSSL never populates it: addrinfo_wrap zero-allocates its nodes, and BIO_ADDRINFO_free's manual path releases only bai_addr and the node itself, so a hand-built node that set this field would leak it.

Owned tail of the node's chain. The head's releaser consumes every linked node: freeaddrinfo for a resolver chain, the manual OPENSSL_free loop in BIO_ADDRINFO_free for the AF_UNIX nodes addrinfo_wrap allocates. No consumer detaches, stores or frees a tail on its own, and BIO_ADDRINFO_next hands it back as const, so projected access must borrow the tail from the head.

types.name: asn1_object_st
types._comment_agent: ASN1_OBJECT conditionally owns its names and encoded bytes according to ASN1_OBJECT_FLAG_DYNAMIC_STRINGS/DATA. Built-in objects borrow immutable static tables, while transient non-dynamic objects may borrow caller storage; all three pointers are nullable. Reviewed 2026-08-26 against crypto/asn1/a_object.c and crypto/objects/obj_dat.{c,h}; the per-field blocks stand. Added evidence: the three flag bits are independent and ASN1_OBJECT_FLAG_DYNAMIC covers only the header allocation, so ASN1_OBJECT_free releases exactly the parts the object owns and is a complete no-op on a built-in. nid_objs is a `static const ASN1_OBJECT[]` whose entries leave flags zero and whose data points into the `static const so[]` blob, so `mutable: false` on sn/ln/data is a hard property of the storage and not just const-qualification -- nothing may be written through an ASN1_OBJECT* that might name a built-in. The header allocation is likewise runtime-conditional: OBJ_dup returns its argument unchanged for a non-dynamic object, and add_object installs OBJ_dup(obj) -- a dynamic copy -- in the added-object hash, which OBJ_nid2obj hands back without transferring. That registry pointer is the one ASN1_OBJECT* that must never be adopted as an owner; every other non-null result may be.

ptr.note: A length-byte immutable OID buffer. DYNAMIC_DATA selects owned storage; built-in objects borrow static table bytes. The source states data remains const after initialization.
Owned and freed when DYNAMIC_STRINGS is set; otherwise built-in objects borrow immutable process-lifetime names. Transient stack objects may also borrow caller strings only for the enclosing call.
Owned and freed when DYNAMIC_STRINGS is set; otherwise built-in objects borrow immutable process-lifetime names. Transient stack objects may also borrow caller strings only for the enclosing call.

types.name: asn1_pctx_st
types._comment_agent: ASN1_PCTX is a plain five-word flag record. The public API keeps its body opaque, allocates it zeroed with ASN1_PCTX_new, releases it with ASN1_PCTX_free, and exposes each scalar through paired getters and setters; it has no pointer fields or clone operation.

types.name: asn1_string_st
types._comment_agent: The data field has runtime-conditional ownership, selected by ASN1_STRING_FLAG_DATA_NOT_OWNED or ASN1_STRING_FLAG_NDEF; length is authoritative and the contents are not generally NUL-terminated. The header's own storage is equally conditional: ASN1_STRING_FLAG_EMBED, set by asn1_primitive_new for ASN1_EMBED template fields, means the struct lives inside a parent allocation and both destructors then release only the data. ASN1_STRING_free and ASN1_STRING_clear_free are ossl_asn1_string_free_internal with clear=0 and clear=1, so either accepts every string the other does and the choice between them is free.

ptr.note: Length-delimited byte buffer, normally owned and released by the ASN1_STRING destructor. Two flags suppress that release and make it a borrowed external buffer: ASN1_STRING_FLAG_DATA_NOT_OWNED, set by ASN1_STRING_new_not_owned, and ASN1_STRING_FLAG_NDEF, set by the streaming PKCS#7 and CMS code for a placeholder pointing into a caller buffer. ASN1_STRING_copy, and therefore ASN1_STRING_dup, allocates a fresh owned buffer and then copies every source flag except EMBED, so a copy of either kind of source owns its buffer while flagged as not owning it and leaks it at free (confirmed under LeakSanitizer). Zero-length strings may carry NULL. Mutating APIs can replace or write the buffer.

types.name: asn1_string_table_st
types._comment_agent: Reviewed 2026-08-23 against crypto/asn1/a_strnid.c, crypto/asn1/tbl_standard.h and include/openssl/asn1.h. A plain scalar record with two storage classes discriminated by the flags field. STABLE_FLAGS_MALLOC marks an entry that stable_get allocated with OPENSSL_zalloc and pushed onto the process-global `stable` stack; ASN1_STRING_TABLE_cleanup releases exactly those through st_free. An entry without the bit is an element of the static const tbl_standard array compiled into the library. ASN1_STRING_TABLE_get casts that constness away and may return either kind, so the result is borrowed, is invalidated by cleanup, and may only be written when it carries STABLE_FLAGS_MALLOC - which is the check stable_get makes before handing a record to ASN1_STRING_TABLE_add for update. STABLE_NO_MASK on the same field tells ASN1_STRING_set_by_NID to use mask directly instead of intersecting it with the global default mask. There is no public per-record destructor.

types.name: asn1_type_st
types._comment_agent: The value union is discriminator-controlled. Heap ASN1_TYPE values created by OpenSSL own active pointer payloads; ASN1_TYPE_free dispatches their release. The common ptr view also appears in non-owning stack temporaries. Pointer arms are nullable; string-shaped payloads are mutable internally, while ASN1_OBJECT payloads are observed immutably. Reviewed 2026-08-23: the ASN1_VALUE spelling of value.asn1_value names the union's generic aliasing slot, not the pointee, so V_ASN1_OTHER and every unenumerated tag carry an ASN1_STRING and only V_ASN1_ANY carries a nested ASN1_TYPE. Reviewed 2026-08-26: ASN1_TYPE_set1 does not always copy. For V_ASN1_OBJECT it calls OBJ_dup (crypto/objects/obj_lib.c), which returns the SOURCE pointer for a non-dynamic object, so the value aliases a static const nid_objs entry that its flag-guarded ASN1_OBJECT_free never releases; for every other tag it calls ASN1_STRING_dup, whose ASN1_STRING_copy propagates ASN1_STRING_FLAG_DATA_NOT_OWNED / ASN1_STRING_FLAG_NDEF, so copying an external-buffer payload yields a duplicate that allocates bytes it is flagged not to own and leaks them on release.

ptr.note: When this union arm is active, a fully constructed ASN1_TYPE owns the pointee and releases it according to the type discriminator; null is permitted.

The union's generic aliasing slot, not a distinct ASN1_VALUE payload: asn1_ex_c2i (tasn_dec.c), asn1_ex_i2c (tasn_enc.c), ossl_asn1_primitive_free (tasn_fre.c) and asn1_print_fsname (tasn_prn.c) all take &typ->value.asn1_value whatever the discriminator is. A fully constructed ASN1_TYPE owns the payload and the discriminator picks the releaser: ASN1_OBJECT_free for V_ASN1_OBJECT; a recursive ossl_asn1_primitive_free plus OPENSSL_free of the nested ASN1_TYPE for V_ASN1_ANY; ASN1_STRING teardown for every other tag, including V_ASN1_OTHER and every tag with no dedicated union member, which asn1_ex_c2i allocates as ASN1_STRING_type_new(tag). V_ASN1_UNDEF (the ASN1_TYPE_new state), V_ASN1_NULL and V_ASN1_BOOLEAN carry no pointer. Null is permitted and the releaser skips it.

types._comment_agent: BIO_meth_new allocates the method and owns its duplicated NUL-terminated name; static method tables borrow static names and callbacks. Callback slots are nullable program-lifetime function pointers and do not own code storage. Review (2026-08-23): re-verified against crypto/bio/bio_meth.c, crypto/bio/bio_lib.c and every BIO_s_*/BIO_f_* definition; the field records above hold. Two facts the field slots cannot carry. (1) The dual owned/borrowed encoding is a property of the TABLE's storage, not just of `name`: every selector returns the address of a file-scope `static const BIO_METHOD` (e.g. null_method in crypto/bio/bss_null.c, corebiometh in crypto/bio/bss_core.c), so those tables live in read-only storage and must be reached only through a borrowed handle -- treating one as an owner would hand BIO_meth_free a .rodata address. types.name: crypto_ex_data_st
types._comment_agent: Field ownership established from crypto/ex_data.c across initialization, duplication, access, mutation, and cleanup paths. Reviewed 2026-08-23: both blocks hold. crypto/ex_data.c is the only file that reads or writes either field, and CRYPTO_free_ex_data is the field disposer (it frees ad->sk and NULLs both fields while keeping the CRYPTO_EX_DATA storage). CRYPTO_dup_ex_data copies from->to but allocates no destination and needs the class index, so it is deliberately not recorded as a cloner.

ptr.note: Borrowed library context installed by ossl_crypto_new_ex_data_ex; NULL selects the default context. CRYPTO_EX_DATA never increments or frees it, and callers must keep the selected context alive while ex-data operations use it; CRYPTO_free_ex_data only clears the field to NULL. The field additionally selects the class registry: every ex-data index resolves through ossl_lib_ctx_get_ex_data_global(ad->ctx), so changing it on a populated value pairs the stored slots with a different context's EX_CALLBACK set.

types.name: engine_st
types._comment_agent: Reviewed: engine_st is an incomplete forward declaration with no fields, so there are no pointer-field findings. Correcting the earlier reason for the absent lifecycle: it is not that this campaign disables deprecated APIs. Engine support has been REMOVED from this tree. include/openssl/engine.h states 'Engine support is gone' and unconditionally redefines ENGINE_new/ENGINE_free/ENGINE_up_ref through the ENGINE_FUNC macros as either deprecated ossl_inline no-op stubs (OPENSSL_ENGINE_STUBS) or bare prototypes whose symbols do not exist; libcrypto.so exports zero ENGINE_* symbols (verified with nm -D --defined-only). types.name: evp_cipher_ctx_st
types._comment_agent: EVP_CIPHER_CTX is publicly opaque. Findings follow evp_enc.c initialization, copy, reset, application-data, legacy cipher-data, and provider-state paths; this wrap wave exposes no field accessors. Reviewed and corrected on one point: the retained cipher is NOT an unconditional keepalive. evp_cipher_init_internal stores the selected record in fetched_cipher behind EVP_CIPHER_up_ref and EVP_CIPHER_CTX_reset releases it with EVP_CIPHER_free, so the obligations match, but for a cached fetch or a legacy static record both are no-ops (evp_cipher_up_ref/evp_cipher_free return early unless origin == EVP_ORIG_DYNAMIC, and the public wrappers additionally short-circuit unless EVP_CIPH_FLAG_NO_STORE). ossl_method_store_cache_get hands back the stored method without taking a reference, so a cached record is owned by the method store of the OSSL_LIB_CTX it was fetched from and an initialized context must not outlive that context. Verified empirically: two fetches from one explicit OSSL_LIB_CTX return the same pointer, three EVP_CIPHER_free calls leave it usable, and after OSSL_LIB_CTX_free the context still holds the released pointer. Same shape as evp_md_ctx_st; latent rather than reachable while no safe OSSL_LIB_CTX_new wrapper exists.

types.name: evp_cipher_st
types._comment_agent: The public EVP_CIPHER surface is opaque, so no field accessor is emitted. Internal inspection shows dynamic records retain prov, own type_name, borrow description and dispatch callbacks from provider-backed algorithm metadata, and use refcnt for dynamic reference counting; legacy static records leave these pointers null. Reviewed and extended: the public EVP_CIPHER_up_ref/EVP_CIPHER_free pair is refcounting ONLY for a record carrying EVP_CIPH_FLAG_NO_STORE, and evp_cipher_up_ref/evp_cipher_free are in turn no-ops unless origin == EVP_ORIG_DYNAMIC. A cached fetch therefore returns a borrowed pointer whose storage the fetching OSSL_LIB_CTX's method store owns (ossl_method_store_cache_get takes no reference), which is why the Rust owner is lifetime-parameterized on the fetching context rather than 'static, and why an owner of a cached record must never be treated as sole ownership.

types.name: evp_mac_ctx_st
types._comment_agent: Reviewed: EVP_MAC_CTX is publicly opaque. A completed context owns provider-specific algorithm state and one public EVP_MAC reference; duplication deep-copies the state and raises the method reference. No private field accessor is exposed by this wrap wave. Adding the verified reason EVP_MAC_CTX_dup needs a guard the KDF equivalent does not: evp_mac_from_algorithm (crypto/evp/mac_meth.c) does not count OSSL_FUNC_MAC_DUPCTX towards fnctxcnt, so meth->dupctx may legitimately be NULL, and EVP_MAC_CTX_dup calls src->meth->dupctx unconditionally once src->algctx != NULL (crypto/evp/mac_lib.c). A safe wrapper must therefore check that dispatch slot before entering the public routine; every MAC in the default provider does supply dupctx, so the guard is reachable only through a third-party provider.

types.name: evp_pkey_st
types._comment_agent: EVP_PKEY is opaque on the published API. Its complete value owns the attribute stack and elements, an acquired EVP_KEYMGMT reference with provider-owned keydata, its thread lock, and the operation-cache stack. The ASN.1 method pointer refers to static method-table storage. references is the object's atomic reference count. Reviewed for lifetime coupling: the struct has no OSSL_LIB_CTX field, but a provider-backed key transitively depends on the library context it was created in through the EVP_KEYMGMT it retains, and nothing in that chain keeps the context alive - EVP_KEYMGMT holds a provider reference, and OSSL_PROVIDER borrows its libctx. Every Rust owner of an EVP_PKEY must therefore carry the creating context's borrow, including one obtained by raising the reference count (X509_get_pubkey, X509_PUBKEY_get) and one produced by EVP_PKEY_dup, which gives the duplicate its source's keymgmt. EVP_PKEY_dup itself only reads its source: the provided path exports through evp_keymgmt_util_export, declared const EVP_PKEY *, and every legacy ameth->copy (rsa/ec/ecx/dh/dsa_pkey_copy) duplicates the source key object without mutating it. Reviewed again for the cached-fetch case: an acquired EVP_KEYMGMT reference does not by itself keep the record alive, because a method reached through evp_generic_fetch is stored in the OSSL_LIB_CTX method store and both EVP_KEYMGMT_up_ref and EVP_KEYMGMT_free are deliberate no-ops for a stored record. That is what makes the context borrow mandatory rather than merely conservative, and it applies to a generated key too: EVP_PKEY_gen assigns the operation's keymgmt through evp_keymgmt_util_assign_pkey -> EVP_PKEY_set_type_by_keymgmt, so EVP_PKEY_keygen and EVP_PKEY_paramgen carry the same dependency as EVP_PKEY_generate and EVP_PKEY_fromdata.

types.name: hostent
types._comment_agent: hostent has no independent lifecycle primitive: nothing in the tree allocates, frees or duplicates an entry or any buffer it points at, so it gets borrowed handles and no owning pointer form. The pointer fields are recorded borrowed with lifetime `self` rather than `static` deliberately. gethostbyname's storage is statically allocated but NOT valid for the life of the program -- the next lookup on the same thread overwrites it in place -- so the name, alias and address buffers are exactly as valid as the entry handle that reached them, and binding them to 'static would be wrong. The other producer, crypto/bio/bio_addr.c's `static const struct hostent he_fallback`, points h_addr_list at file-scope statics and is itself const, i.e. read-only storage; between the two, no producer in this tree yields a writable entry, so an exclusive handle is only ever legitimate over caller-owned storage. BIO_lookup_ex is the only in-tree field reader: it takes h_addrtype, h_length and h_addr_list, and walks the address vector without a NULL check on the vector itself. h_name and h_aliases are never read in-tree; their records describe the public struct hostent surface rather than observed OpenSSL behaviour.

BIO_lookup_ex reads the vector and every element but writes through neither, and dereferences the vector pointer without a NULL check -- nullable stays true because the public struct permits NULL, so a Rust getter should hand back an Option rather than inherit that assumption.

types._comment_agent: in6_addr is a by-value 16-byte address with no pointer fields, no refcount and no lifecycle primitive. Its three C union members alias the same 16 bytes: s6_addr keeps the network-order octets, while s6_addr16 and s6_addr32 reinterpret those bytes in host order, so the word views are byte-swapped against the wire on a little-endian target. Like in_addr it is read through BIO_ADDR_rawmake's untyped `const void *where` (`*(struct in6_addr *)where`, crypto/bio/bio_addr.c:158), so a wrapper must not assume the union's 4-byte alignment: the byte view is alignment-free, but the 16- and 32-bit views need unaligned loads and stores.

types.name: in_addr

Its single s_addr field is network-order scalar data; there is no pointer field, no refcount and no lifecycle primitive, so it needs no owner and no releaser. types._comment_agent: OBJ_NAME records own only their header allocation inside o_names.c: OBJ_NAME_add OPENSSL_mallocs one, and OBJ_NAME_add (on replacement), OBJ_NAME_remove and OBJ_NAME_cleanup OPENSSL_free it after running the class's registered free_func on the name/data pair. There is no public per-record constructor, destructor or clone. `alias` discriminates `data`: a non-zero alias makes data the borrowed name of another entry of the same class (OBJ_NAME_get feeds it back as its next lookup key), and a zero alias makes it the class's registered payload, an erased pointer that is NOT a string -- EVP_add_cipher and EVP_add_digest store (const char *)cipher / (const char *)md, and do_all_cipher_fn/do_all_md_fn cast it straight back. `type` and `name` are the hash key.

ptr.note: Discriminated by the sibling `alias` field, and only one arm is a string; the record cannot hold both, so `string: true` covers the alias arm and this note carries the other. alias != 0: `data` is the caller-managed NUL-terminated name of another entry of the same class, which OBJ_NAME_get assigns to `on.name` and looks up again (o_names.c:172). alias == 0: `data` is the registered payload, an erased pointer whose concrete type is fixed by `type` -- `const EVP_CIPHER *` from EVP_add_cipher, `const EVP_MD *` from EVP_add_digest, arbitrary for a class from OBJ_NAME_new_index -- and do_all_cipher_fn/do_all_md_fn (crypto/evp/names.c:201-252) and get_legacy_cipher_names (crypto/core_namemap.c:409) cast it back. Reading that arm as a C string is an out-of-bounds read: it is not NUL-terminated. Either arm is stored without copying and OBJ_NAME_add does not validate it; NULL is reachable and reported by OBJ_NAME_get as `not registered`. Any external storage is governed by the class's optional free_func, never by OBJ_NAME itself.

OBJ_NAME_add stores the caller's const NUL-terminated name without copying it; registered callbacks receive that borrowed pointer. Every reader dereferences it unconditionally -- obj_name_cmp hands it to OPENSSL_strcasecmp, which derefs without a NULL check, and apps/enc.c:860 indexes it -- so a non-NULL name is the invariant the registry relies on. It is not enforced: OBJ_NAME_add takes the pointer unchecked, and EVP_add_cipher / EVP_add_digest pass an unchecked OBJ_nid2sn / OBJ_nid2ln result, which is NULL for a nid outside the object table (obj_dat.c:279-291). ossl_lh_strcasehash tolerates NULL, so such an entry can be inserted and later reached, making the NULL state observable rather than impossible: nullable, with every consumer requiring the non-NULL case.

types.name: ossl_lib_ctx_st
types._comment_agent: Reviewed against crypto/context.c for the ossl_lib_ctx_st wrapper. No field stores a reference count: the type has exactly one release primitive, OSSL_LIB_CTX_free, and no up_ref or dup anywhere in the tree, so its Rust lifecycle is CDropped alone. OSSL_LIB_CTX_free tolerates null and silently retains a context that is the CALLING THREAD's current default: ossl_lib_ctx_is_default_nocreate() compares against check_default_context(), which is the thread-local set through OSSL_LIB_CTX_set0_default when one is installed and the static default_context_int otherwise - so the two cases are alternatives, not a union, and freeing a context that a DIFFERENT thread installed as its default really releases it. Freeing the calling thread's own default leaks rather than corrupting. types.name: ossl_param_st
types._comment_agent: OSSL_PARAM is a by-value descriptor with no independent destructor. Both pointer fields are borrowed; data_type and data_size determine the runtime interpretation and return_size is mutable result metadata. Reviewed against include/openssl/params.h: a real descriptor built by OSSL_PARAM_DEFN starts at return_size = OSSL_PARAM_UNMODIFIED ((size_t)-1), but the array terminator OSSL_PARAM_END - the value OSSL_PARAM_construct_end returns - is exactly { NULL, 0, NULL, 0, 0 }, so its return_size is 0. Only key == NULL terminates an array; every C scanner in the tree walks 'for (p = params; p->key != NULL; p++)' and never reads the terminator's other fields. An array pointer handed to C must therefore be derived from a borrow covering the whole run through its terminator, not from its first element. Second review pass, against crypto/params.c and crypto/params_dup.c: data_size is the byte capacity of data ONLY for the value-carrying data types. OSSL_PARAM_UTF8_PTR (6) and OSSL_PARAM_OCTET_PTR (7) store a single void * at data and use data_size for the referent, so a byte view of data_size bytes at data is out of bounds for them - any wrapper's byte accessor must be discriminator-aware. Also confirmed the array-level ownership shape: OSSL_PARAM_dup allocates one backing block for every duplicated key and data run and records it on the terminator with data_type OSSL_PARAM_ALLOCATED_END; OSSL_PARAM_free walks to that terminator, frees the block, then frees the array. Individual descriptors of a duplicated array are therefore still non-owning, and clearing one descriptor's data neither leaks nor double-frees. Third review pass: no correction to the recorded C semantics; the discriminator coupling above is confirmed against crypto/params.c (get_ptr_internal_skip_checks, set_ptr_internal) and crypto/params_dup.c, and is now enforced by the Rust wrapper's safe constructors and setters rather than only documented by them.

ptr.note: Runtime-discriminated caller-managed storage. INTEGER/UNSIGNED/REAL can name scalar native values, UTF8_STRING/OCTET_STRING name data_size bytes, and UTF8_PTR/OCTET_PTR name a lone pointer slot. Cardinality is NOT uniformly data_size: crypto/params.c reaches the two _PTR types as *(const void **)p->data (set_ptr_internal, get_ptr_internal_skip_checks), so for them data_size bounds the REFERENT and no run of data_size bytes exists at data; only the value-carrying types make data_size the byte capacity of data. Setters write through it; NULL is valid for size queries. The descriptor itself never releases the referent; even OSSL_PARAM_dup places copied bytes in one array-owned backing block, recorded on the terminator as OSSL_PARAM_ALLOCATED_END and released by OSSL_PARAM_free, rather than making each field an independent owner. Third review pass: the pointer-slot coupling is a REACHABILITY fact, not only a documentation one. Provider set_ctx_params handlers read a caller-supplied descriptor through OSSL_PARAM_get_utf8_string_ptr / get_octet_string_ptr (providers/common/provider_util.c:180-208, providers/implementations/keymgmt/*, storemgmt/file_store.c), and get_ctx_params handlers write one through OSSL_PARAM_set_octet_ptr (ciphercommon.c:606, asymciphers/rsa_enc.c:426, exchange/dh_exch.c:505, exchange/ecdh_exch.c:399), so any caller that can choose data_type and data independently makes C load or store a whole void * through storage that need be neither pointer-sized nor pointer-aligned. Confirmed with EVP_KDF_CTX_set_params on KBKDF's 'mac' parameter: UBSan reports 'crypto/params.c:1480 load of misaligned address ... for type const void *'. Note also that ossl_param_set_secure_block (crypto/params_dup.c:53) leaves the OSSL_PARAM_ALLOCATED_END terminator of a duplicated array with data = the secure block and data_size = that block's byte size, so the value-carrying coupling does hold for it.

types.name: ossl_provider_st
types._comment_agent: Reviewed the complete private layout and all field uses in crypto/provider_core.c. The public API exposes only an opaque forward declaration, so these facts document its C lifecycle rather than authorizing field projection in Rust. Reviewed for lifetime coupling and release classes: libctx is a borrowed back-pointer, so a provider reference does not retain its library context and an owner must not outlive it - when the context is freed its provider store releases the store's references, leaving any surviving provider's libctx dangling. Two distinct release classes exist for the same pointer: the public OSSL_PROVIDER_unload(prov) = ossl_provider_deactivate(prov, 1) then ossl_provider_free(prov), which returns 0 WITHOUT freeing when deactivation fails (a leak, never a double release), and the internal ossl_provider_free(prov), which consumes a reference carrying no activation. ossl_provider_up_ref adds a reference without an activation and, for a child provider, mirrors it onto the parent through ossl_provider_up_ref_parent; it is not the inverse of OSSL_PROVIDER_unload. Third review pass, re-verified: OSSL_PROVIDER_unload (crypto/provider.c:71) is still ossl_provider_deactivate(prov, 1) followed by ossl_provider_free, returning 0 without freeing when deactivation fails, and ossl_provider_up_ref remains reference-only. No correction. Fourth review pass (wrap review of the Rust representation) adds the aliasing fact the earlier passes left out: OSSL_PROVIDER_load is not a constructor. OSSL_PROVIDER_try_load_ex (crypto/provider.c:18) starts at ossl_provider_find(libctx, name, 0), which returns the provider store's existing entry after ossl_provider_up_ref; only a miss reaches ossl_provider_new. It then activates and returns that same object, and add_to_store can even replace the caller's fresh provider with the concurrently registered 'actual' one. So two successful loads of one name in one library context yield the SAME OSSL_PROVIDER * with two activations and two references, each carrying its own OSSL_PROVIDER_unload obligation. An active public handle is therefore a share, never a sole allocation: the Rust owner is refcount::SharedRef (SharedOsslProvider<'a>), and adopting a load result into ffibox::CBox, whose from_raw demands unique ownership and whose as_mut hands out an exclusive handle, would assert exclusivity the C API does not grant. Confirmed by a unit test in crustify/rust/libcrypto/src/provider/provider_core.rs that loads 'default' twice into a private context and compares the two pointers.

Consumes a nullable allocation obtained from CRYPTO_secure_malloc / CRYPTO_secure_zalloc, whichever allocator actually served it; applies to scalar storage, counted buffers, and strings. NULL returns before anything else, so a null pointer is safe whatever num says. Like CRYPTO_secure_free it dispatches on the pointer's address through CRYPTO_secure_allocated -> sh_allocated (WITHIN_ARENA), and the two routines differ ONLY on the ordinary-allocation branch. Arena branch: num is IGNORED and the cleanse length is sh_actual_size(ptr), the whole buddy block (the request rounded up), so the erasure is at least what the caller asked for and the call is indistinguishable from CRYPTO_secure_free. Ordinary branch: num is exactly the OPENSSL_cleanse length (crypto/mem_clr.c, an unelidable memset) - caller-asserted, never derived from the allocation, so it must not exceed the live bytes, and bytes past it survive into free(). Unlike CRYPTO_clear_free there is no `if (num)` guard around the cleanse, but OPENSSL_cleanse(ptr, 0) is a no-op memset, so num == 0 leaves the call equivalent to CRYPTO_secure_free. Release then goes through CRYPTO_free on that branch, the same allocator CRYPTO_secure_free uses there, so cleansing changes what the storage holds and never which allocator reclaims it: a buffer is interchangeable between CRYPTO_secure_free and CRYPTO_secure_clear_free owners. Under OPENSSL_NO_SECURE_MEMORY only the ordinary branch remains. Release is not guaranteed to happen: on the arena branch a failing CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock(sec_malloc_lock) returns without freeing, leaking the block. CRYPTO_secure_free never reads the (file, line) pair itself, and the arena branch discards it entirely; it reaches CRYPTO_free only on the ordinary-allocation branch, which forwards it verbatim to an application-installed CRYPTO_free_fn and otherwise calls free(ptr) alone (crypto/mem.c). NULL is inside that contract for the same reason it is for CRYPTO_free. Consumes a nullable allocation obtained from CRYPTO_secure_malloc / CRYPTO_secure_zalloc, whichever allocator actually served it; applies to scalar storage, counted buffers, and strings. NULL returns before anything else. The branch is chosen from the pointer itself, not from anything the caller asserts: CRYPTO_secure_allocated -> sh_allocated is an arena address-range test (WITHIN_ARENA in crypto/mem_sec.c). Arena storage is cleansed over sh_actual_size(ptr) - the whole buddy block, i.e. the request rounded up to a power of two - and returned to the secure heap. Anything else is released through CRYPTO_free with its bytes INTACT: this routine never cleanses ordinary storage, and that is the path every allocation takes while the secure heap is down, because CRYPTO_secure_malloc/zalloc fall through to CRYPTO_malloc/CRYPTO_zalloc before CRYPTO_secure_malloc_init succeeds and after CRYPTO_secure_malloc_done. Under OPENSSL_NO_SECURE_MEMORY the entire body is that fallback. Consequences for pairing: this is a strict superset of CRYPTO_free - an ordinary OpenSSL allocation is released correctly here, only uncleansed - while the reverse is invalid, since CRYPTO_free would hand an arena address to free() or to an installed CRYPTO_free_fn. A buffer that may be secure must therefore be released by CRYPTO_secure_free or CRYPTO_secure_clear_free. Release is also not guaranteed to happen: on the arena branch a failing CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock(sec_malloc_lock) returns without freeing, leaking the block.

The type's only release primitive: for a heap context it runs ossl_provider_deinit_child (child contexts), context_deinit and OPENSSL_free, and no other path frees an OSSL_LIB_CTX. It is total rather than exclusively owning: it returns early for NULL and for ossl_lib_ctx_is_default_nocreate(ctx), which matches BOTH the static default_context_int AND any context the calling thread installed as its default through OSSL_LIB_CTX_set0_default. The second case is the corner: that context is an ordinary heap context the caller owns, so the retained path is not limited to the process-global default, and freeing a current default leaks the context instead of corrupting it. The type has no reference count and no up_ref or dup, so this is the whole lifecycle. Rust owners only adopt constructor results and never the default, which keeps the owning path exact.

The provider is not up-refed; RAND stores its bare address alongside a strdup of its name (only the name is the 'set1' copy). NULL disables the override. The stored address is kept alive by the provider store of the provider's OWN libctx, not by RAND: provider_deactivate deregisters via ossl_rand_check_random_provider_on_unload(prov->libctx, prov), so registering a provider loaded against a DIFFERENT context is never cleared here and dangles once that context is freed - RAND_bytes_ex/RAND_priv_bytes_ex then dereference released storage. Consumes a nullable byte buffer owned by the caller. Declared static ossl_inline in an internal header, so there is no linkable symbol to call: a Rust surface is a native translation of the branch it selects, not an FFI wrap. Both branches release through CRYPTO_free - OPENSSL_clear_free(ptr, size) -> CRYPTO_clear_free -> CRYPTO_free when OPENSSL_PEDANTIC_ZEROIZATION is defined, OPENSSL_free(ptr) -> CRYPTO_free otherwise - so the storage is an ordinary OpenSSL allocation whichever way the module is configured and only the cleansing differs; a buffer therefore crosses between C and a Rust owner in either build. size is read only on the pedantic branch, where it becomes the OPENSSL_cleanse length and must be the buffer's live byte count; the default branch ignores it, so a wrong size is inert there and harmful only under pedantic zeroization. Every in-tree caller is crypto/ffc/ffc_params.c (ossl_ffc_params_cleanup, ossl_ffc_params_set_seed, ossl_ffc_params_copy), passing params->seed with params->seedlen: an OPENSSL_memdup buffer of exactly seedlen bytes, or the NULL/0 pair ossl_ffc_params_init leaves behind. OPENSSL_PEDANTIC_ZEROIZATION is a supported configuration exercised daily in CI (.github/workflows/run-checker-daily.yml), not dead code.
